description: Hey everyone, I'm Ashwin! I'm participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge and working on the astronaut health monitoring challenge. I'm well-versed in a variety of technical languages and have extensive experience researching space biology. I'm looking for teammates interested in biology, bioinformatics, coding, AI, or data visualization to help build an interactive tool that helps astronauts monitor and understand their health during long-duration space missions.
summary: Blink is an astronomical discovery platform that leverages NASA's SPHEREx spectrophotometric survey data to identify, track, and characterize high-proper-motion celestial objects. By processing observations across 102 infrared spectral bands and multiple temporal epochs, Blink integrates multi-wavelength image registration, precision astrometric measurements, and a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) to distinguish genuine astronomical motion from stationary sources and observational artifacts. Its spectral classification pipeline employs template fitting and photometric analysis to characterize objects, including brown dwarfs, stars, and extragalactic sources. The platform incorporates Gaia DR3 cross-validation to establish measurement accuracy and employs machine learning inference to prioritize potential discoveries. Through interactive temporal visualizations, difference imaging, motion analysis, and spectral decomposition, Blink transforms complex astronomical datasets into an accessible discovery environment, accelerating the identification and characterization of previously overlooked infrared sources.
details:
Blink is a full-stack astronomical discovery platform that combines NASA's SPHEREx infrared survey data, computational astrophysics, and machine learning to detect, track, and classify moving celestial objects. The system processes multi-epoch observations across 102 infrared wavelength bands, using image registration, effective point-spread function (ePSF) fitting, and astrometric analysis to measure proper motion. Our custom convolutional neural network, MoverNet, identifies potential moving objects, while spectral template fitting classifies them as stars, brown dwarfs, galaxies, or solar-system objects.

We developed Blink using Python (FastAPI, Astropy, Photutils, PyTorch), TypeScript, Next.js, and ONNX Runtime Web. Its creative approach modernizes Clyde Tombaugh's original blink comparator by combining interactive temporal imaging with automated machine learning detection directly in the browser. Validated against ESA's Gaia DR3 catalogue, our system achieved a CNN ROC AUC of 0.87 on previously unseen astronomical fields.

Beyond detection, Blink provides four visualization modes: Flipbook, Stack, Difference, and Motion, allowing users to examine temporal changes and distinguish genuine movement from background noise. Its spectral analysis reconstructs 102-channel infrared spectra to identify molecular absorption features associated with different celestial object classes. We also account for observational artifacts, source blending, and variable stars to minimize false positives. Ultimately, Blink democratizes advanced infrared astronomy by transforming complex telescope data into an accessible discovery platform for researchers and citizen scientists.
